THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT FACT IN THIS FILE — THE CLOSING TIME
- Brazilian polls CLOSE AT 17:00 BRASILIA TIME, WHICH IS 20:00 GMT.
- Al Jazeera states both: 5:00 pm local Brasilia time, 20:00 GMT/UTC.
- CONSEQUENCE FOR A 19:15 GMT PUBLICATION: Brazilian polls will STILL BE OPEN when you publish, with about 45 minutes of voting left. There can be no turnout total, no result, no declaration, no concession and no claim of victory. ANY of those in tonight's column would be invented. Brazil is a "still voting" diary line tonight, not a result.
- Eligible voters: "nearly 160 million".
- The first round was 4 October.

If you want to print a time, attribute it, or write "polls close this evening, with results expected within hours".

ELECTORATE FIGURE — THREE-WAY CONFLICT, DO NOT AVERAGE
- Al Jazeera live blog, 25 Oct: "nearly 160 million" eligible voters.
- Guardian, 25 Oct 14:41 GMT: "an electorate of 159 million".
- Guardian, 24 Oct 21:10 GMT: "Nearly 159m Brazilians will vote in the election's runoff on Sunday".
- Al Jazeera, 4 Oct: "About 160 million registered voters".
RECOMMENDED SAFE FORM: "about 159 million" (Guardian) or "nearly 160 million" (Al Jazeera), attributed. Do not write a single unattributed figure.
